description: The line plot illustrates the Average Success Rate (ASR) across different trigger words, with the x-axis representing the trigger words—“bb,” “mb,” “cf,” “beautiful,” “excellent,” “gorgeous,” “wonderful,” “brilliant,” “stunning,” and “beautifully”—and the y-axis showing the ASR on a scale from 0.2 to 0.9. Three distinct lines represent different methods: “start” (green with circle markers), “random” (orange with cross markers), and “end” (purple with circle markers). The “start” method begins at an ASR of approximately 0.2 for “bb,” rises sharply to about 0.74 for “mb,” drops to 0.4 for “cf,” and then generally increases, peaking at 0.92 for “stunning” before slightly declining to 0.88 for “beautifully.” The “random” method starts at 0.54 for “bb,” decreases to 0.2 for “cf,” then rises sharply to 0.91 for “beautifully,” with a peak of 0.82 for “stunning.” The “end” method begins at 0.52 for “bb,” increases to 0.84 for “cf,” then fluctuates, peaking at 0.92 for “wonderful,” and ending at 0.85 for “beautifully.” The “random” method shows the highest ASR for “beautifully,” while the “end” method achieves the highest ASR for “wonderful.”
